speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; to help your newborn who is presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth, I need to ask some questions. Has the infant been feeding well, and has there been any fever or vomiting since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE).

The clinical picture of a 31-week preterm infant born after chorioamnionitis, with low Apgar scores, and now presenting with seizures and lethargy at 72 hours of age is highly concerning for HIE or early-onset sepsis. I need to evaluate for acute injury and infection. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Blood_Culture, CSF_Analysis, Electrolytes, Glucose, Coagulation_Profile. REQUEST IMAGES: Head_Ultrasound, Brain_MRI.
